  1677→// HandleTurnEnd dispatches strategy-specific actions emitted when an agent turn ends.
  1678→// The primary job is to finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
  1679→//
  1680→// During a turn, PostCommit writes provisional transcript data (whatever was available
  1681→// at commit time). HandleTurnEnd replaces that with the complete session transcript
  1682→// (from prompt to stop event), ensuring every checkpoint has the full context.
  1683→//
  1684→
  1685→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) HandleTurnEnd(state *SessionState) error {
  1686→	// Finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
  1687→	//
  1688→	// IMPORTANT: This is best-effort - errors are logged but don't fail the hook.
  1689→	// Failing here would prevent session cleanup and could leave state inconsistent.
  1690→	// The provisional transcript from PostCommit is already persisted, so the
  1691→	// checkpoint isn't lost - it just won't have the complete transcript.
  1692→	errCount := s.finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state)
  1693→	if errCount > 0 {
  1694→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  1695→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "HandleTurnEnd completed with errors (best-effort)",
  1696→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1697→			slog.Int("error_count", errCount),
  1698→		)
  1699→	}
  1700→	return nil
  1701→}
  1702→
  1703→// finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints replaces the provisional transcript in each checkpoint
  1704→// created during this turn with the full session transcript.
  1705→//
  1706→// This is called at turn end (stop hook). During the turn, PostCommit wrote whatever
  1707→// transcript was available at commit time. Now we have the complete transcript and
  1708→// replace it so every checkpoint has the full prompt-to-stop context.
  1709→//
  1710→// Returns the number of errors encountered (best-effort: continues processing on error).
  1711→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state *SessionState) int {
  1712→	if len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) == 0 {
  1713→		return 0 // No mid-turn commits to finalize
  1714→	}
  1715→
  1716→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  1717→
  1718→	logging.Info(logCtx, "finalizing turn checkpoints with full transcript",
  1719→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1720→		slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs)),
  1721→	)
  1722→
  1723→	errCount := 0
  1724→
  1725→	// Read full transcript from live transcript file
  1726→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
  1727→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: no transcript path, skipping",
  1728→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1729→		)
  1730→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1731→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1732→	}
  1733→
  1734→	fullTranscript, err := os.ReadFile(state.TranscriptPath)
  1735→	if err != nil || len(fullTranscript) == 0 {
  1736→		msg := "finalize: empty transcript, skipping"
  1737→		if err != nil {
  1738→			msg = "finalize: failed to read transcript, skipping"
  1739→		}
  1740→		logging.Warn(logCtx, msg,
  1741→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1742→			slog.String("transcript_path", state.TranscriptPath),
  1743→			slog.Any("error", err),
  1744→		)
  1745→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1746→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1747→	}
  1748→
  1749→	// Extract prompts and context from the full transcript
  1750→	prompts := extractUserPrompts(state.AgentType, string(fullTranscript))
  1751→	contextBytes := generateContextFromPrompts(prompts)
  1752→
  1753→	// Redact secrets before writing — matches WriteCommitted behavior.
  1754→	// The live transcript on disk contains raw content; redaction must happen
  1755→	// before anything is persisted to the metadata branch.
  1756→	fullTranscript, err = redact.JSONLBytes(fullTranscript)
  1757→	if err != nil {
  1758→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: transcript redaction failed, skipping",
  1759→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1760→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1761→		)
  1762→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1763→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1764→	}
  1765→	for i, p := range prompts {
  1766→		prompts[i] = redact.String(p)
  1767→	}
  1768→	contextBytes = redact.Bytes(contextBytes)
  1769→
  1770→	// Open repository and create checkpoint store
  1771→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
  1772→	if err != nil {
  1773→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to open repository",
  1774→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1775→		)
  1776→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1777→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1778→	}
  1779→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)

  1782→	for _, cpIDStr := range state.TurnCheckpointIDs {
  1783→		cpID, parseErr := id.NewCheckpointID(cpIDStr)

  1785→			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: invalid checkpoint ID, skipping",
  1786→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1787→				slog.String("error", parseErr.Error()),
  1788→			)
  1789→			errCount++
  1790→			continue
  1791→		}
  1792→
  1793→		updateErr := store.UpdateCommitted(context.Background(), checkpoint.UpdateCommittedOptions{
  1794→			CheckpointID: cpID,
  1795→			SessionID:    state.SessionID,
  1796→			Transcript:   fullTranscript,
  1797→			Prompts:      prompts,
  1798→			Context:      contextBytes,
  1799→			Agent:        state.AgentType,
  1800→		})

  1803→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1804→				slog.String("error", updateErr.Error()),
  1805→			)

  1808→		}

  1811→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),

  1813→		)
  1814→	}

  1817→	// already set correctly by PostCommit: condenseAndUpdateState sets it to the total
  1818→	// transcript lines when condensing, and carryForwardToNewShadowBranch resets it to 0
  1819→	// when carry-forward is active. Overwriting here would break carry-forward by making
  1820→	// sessionHasNewContent think the transcript is fully consumed (no growth).

  1826→// filesChangedInCommit returns the set of files changed in a commit by diffing against its parent.
  1827→func filesChangedInCommit(commit *object.Commit) map[string]struct{} {
  1828→	result := make(map[string]struct{})
  1829→
  1830→	commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
  1831→	if err != nil {
  1832→		return result
  1833→	}
  1834→
  1835→	var parentTree *object.Tree
  1836→	if commit.NumParents() > 0 {
  1837→		parent, err := commit.Parent(0)
  1838→		if err != nil {
  1839→			return result
  1840→		}
  1841→		parentTree, err = parent.Tree()
  1842→		if err != nil {
  1843→			return result
  1844→		}
  1845→	}
  1846→
  1847→	if parentTree == nil {
  1848→		// Initial commit — all files are new
  1849→		if iterErr := commitTree.Files().ForEach(func(f *object.File) error {
  1850→			result[f.Name] = struct{}{}
  1851→			return nil
  1852→		}); iterErr != nil {
  1853→			return result
  1854→		}
  1855→		return result
  1856→	}
  1857→
  1858→	changes, err := parentTree.Diff(commitTree)
  1859→	if err != nil {
  1860→		return result
  1861→	}
  1862→	for _, change := range changes {
  1863→		name := change.To.Name
  1864→		if name == "" {
  1865→			name = change.From.Name
  1866→		}
  1867→		result[name] = struct{}{}
  1868→	}
  1869→	return result
  1870→}
  1871→
  1872→// subtractFiles returns files that are NOT in the exclude set.
  1873→func subtractFiles(files []string, exclude map[string]struct{}) []string {
  1874→	var remaining []string
  1875→	for _, f := range files {
  1876→		if _, excluded := exclude[f]; !excluded {
  1877→			remaining = append(remaining, f)
  1878→		}
  1879→	}
  1880→	return remaining
  1881→}
  1882→
  1883→// carryForwardToNewShadowBranch creates a new shadow branch at the current HEAD
  1884→// containing the remaining uncommitted files and all session metadata.
  1885→// This enables the next commit to get its own unique checkpoint.
  1886→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
  1887→	logCtx context.Context,
  1888→	repo *git.Repository,
  1889→	state *SessionState,
  1890→	remainingFiles []string,
  1891→) {
  1892→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
  1893→
  1894→	// Don't include metadata directory in carry-forward. The carry-forward branch
  1895→	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
  1896→	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
  1897→	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
  1898→	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
  1899→		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
  1900→		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
  1901→		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
  1902→		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
  1903→		MetadataDir:       "",
  1904→		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
  1905→		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
  1906→		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
  1907→	})
  1908→	if err != nil {
  1909→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward failed",
  1910→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1911→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1912→		)
  1913→		return
  1914→	}
  1915→	if result.Skipped {
  1916→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
  1917→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1918→		)
  1919→		return
  1920→	}
  1921→
  1922→	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
  1923→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
  1924→	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:
  1925→	// - Pro: Each checkpoint is independently readable without needing to stitch together
  1926→	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history
  1927→	// - Con: For long sessions with multiple partial commits, each checkpoint includes
  1928→	//   the full transcript, which could be large
  1929→	// An alternative would be incremental checkpoints (only new content since last condensation),
  1930→	// but this would complicate checkpoint retrieval and require careful tracking of dependencies.
  1931→	state.StepCount = 1
  1932→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0
  1933→	state.LastCheckpointID = ""
  1934→	// NOTE: TurnCheckpointIDs is intentionally NOT cleared here. Those checkpoint
  1935→	// IDs from earlier in the turn still need finalization with the full transcript
  1936→	// when HandleTurnEnd runs at stop time.
  1937→
  1938→	logging.Info(logCtx, "post-commit: carried forward remaining files",
  1939→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1940→		slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remainingFiles)),
  1941→	)
  1942→}

   263→		CheckpointTranscriptStart:   state.CheckpointTranscriptStart,
   264→		TokenUsage:                  sessionData.TokenUsage,
   265→		InitialAttribution:          attribution,
   266→		Summary:                     summary,
   267→	}); err != nil {
   268→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write checkpoint metadata: %w", err)
   269→	}
   270→
   271→	return &CondenseResult{
   272→		CheckpointID:         checkpointID,
   273→		SessionID:            state.SessionID,
   274→		CheckpointsCount:     state.StepCount,
   275→		FilesTouched:         sessionData.FilesTouched,
   276→		TotalTranscriptLines: sessionData.FullTranscriptLines,
   277→	}, nil
   278→}

   280→func calculateSessionAttributions(repo *git.Repository, shadowRef *plumbing.Reference, sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState) *cpkg.InitialAttribution {
   281→	// Calculate initial attribution using accumulated prompt attribution data.
   282→	// This uses user edits captured at each prompt start (before agent works),
   283→	// plus any user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head).
   284→	//
   285→	// When shadowRef is nil (agent committed mid-turn before SaveStep),
   286→	// HEAD is used as the shadow tree. This is correct because the agent's
   287→	// commit IS HEAD — there are no user edits between agent work and commit.
   288→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   289→
   290→	headRef, headErr := repo.Head()
   291→	if headErr != nil {
   292→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD",
   293→			slog.String("error", headErr.Error()))
   294→		return nil
   295→	}
   296→
   297→	headCommit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(headRef.Hash())
   298→	if commitErr != nil {
   299→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD commit",
   300→			slog.String("error", commitErr.Error()))
   301→		return nil
   302→	}
   303→
   304→	headTree, treeErr := headCommit.Tree()
   305→	if treeErr != nil {
   306→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD tree",
   307→			slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
   308→		return nil
   309→	}
   310→
   311→	// Get shadow tree: from shadow branch if available, otherwise HEAD (agent committed directly).
   312→	var shadowTree *object.Tree
   313→	if shadowRef != nil {
   314→		shadowCommit, shadowErr := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
   315→		if shadowErr != nil {
   316→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow commit",
   317→				slog.String("error", shadowErr.Error()),
   318→				slog.String("shadow_ref", shadowRef.Hash().String()))
   319→			return nil
   320→		}
   321→		var shadowTreeErr error
   322→		shadowTree, shadowTreeErr = shadowCommit.Tree()
   323→		if shadowTreeErr != nil {
   324→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow tree",
   325→				slog.String("error", shadowTreeErr.Error()))
   326→			return nil
   327→		}
   328→	} else {
   329→		// No shadow branch: agent committed mid-turn. Use HEAD as shadow
   330→		// because the agent's work is the commit itself.
   331→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: using HEAD as shadow (no shadow branch)")
   332→		shadowTree = headTree
   333→	}
   334→
   335→	// Get base tree (state before session started)
   336→	var baseTree *object.Tree
   337→	attrBase := state.AttributionBaseCommit
   338→	if attrBase == "" {
   339→		attrBase = state.BaseCommit // backward compat
   340→	}
   341→	if baseCommit, baseErr := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(attrBase)); baseErr == nil {
   342→		if tree, baseTErr := baseCommit.Tree(); baseTErr == nil {
   343→			baseTree = tree
   344→		} else {
   345→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base tree unavailable",
   346→				slog.String("error", baseTErr.Error()))
   347→		}
   348→	} else {
   349→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base commit unavailable",
   350→			slog.String("error", baseErr.Error()),
   351→			slog.String("attribution_base", attrBase))
   352→	}
   353→
   354→	// Log accumulated prompt attributions for debugging
   355→	var totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved int
   356→	for i, pa := range state.PromptAttributions {
   357→		totalUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
   358→		totalUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
   359→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution data",
   360→			slog.Int("checkpoint", pa.CheckpointNumber),
   361→			slog.Int("user_added", pa.UserLinesAdded),
   362→			slog.Int("user_removed", pa.UserLinesRemoved),
   363→			slog.Int("agent_added", pa.AgentLinesAdded),
   364→			slog.Int("agent_removed", pa.AgentLinesRemoved),
   365→			slog.Int("index", i))
   366→	}
   367→
   368→	attribution := CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(
   369→		baseTree,
   370→		shadowTree,
   371→		headTree,
   372→		sessionData.FilesTouched,
   373→		state.PromptAttributions,
   374→	)
   375→
   376→	if attribution != nil {
   377→		logging.Info(logCtx, "attribution calculated",
   378→			slog.Int("agent_lines", attribution.AgentLines),
   379→			slog.Int("human_added", attribution.HumanAdded),
   380→			slog.Int("human_modified", attribution.HumanModified),
   381→			slog.Int("human_removed", attribution.HumanRemoved),
   382→			slog.Int("total_committed", attribution.TotalCommitted),
   383→			slog.Float64("agent_percentage", attribution.AgentPercentage),
   384→			slog.Int("accumulated_user_added", totalUserAdded),
   385→			slog.Int("accumulated_user_removed", totalUserRemoved),
   386→			slog.Int("files_touched", len(sessionData.FilesTouched)))
   387→	}
   388→
   389→	return attribution
   390→}

   392→// extractSessionData extracts session data from the shadow branch.
   393→// filesTouched is the list of files tracked during the session (from SessionState.FilesTouched).
   394→// agentType identifies the agent (e.g., "Gemini CLI", "Claude Code") to determine transcript format.
   395→// liveTranscriptPath, when non-empty and readable, is preferred over the shadow branch copy.
   396→// This handles the case where SaveStep was skipped (no code changes) but the transcript
   397→// continued growing — the shadow branch copy would be stale.
   398→// checkpointTranscriptStart is the line offset (Claude) or message index (Gemini) where the current checkpoint began.
   399→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractSessionData(repo *git.Repository, shadowRef plumbing.Hash, sessionID string, filesTouched []string, agentType agent.AgentType, liveTranscriptPath string, checkpointTranscriptStart int, isActive bool) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
   400→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef)
   401→	if err != nil {
   402→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   403→	}
   404→
   405→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   406→	if err != nil {
   407→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   408→	}
   409→
   410→	data := &ExtractedSessionData{}
   411→	// sessionID is already an "entire session ID" (with date prefix)
   412→	metadataDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
   413→
   414→	// Extract transcript — prefer the live file when available, fall back to shadow branch.
   415→	// The shadow branch copy may be stale if the last turn ended without code changes
   416→	// (SaveStep is only called when there are file modifications).
   417→	var fullTranscript string
   418→	if liveTranscriptPath != "" {
   419→		// Ensure transcript file exists (OpenCode creates it lazily via `opencode export`).
   420→		// Only wait for flush when the session is active — for idle/ended sessions the
   421→		// transcript is already fully flushed (the Stop hook completed the flush).
   422→		if isActive {
   423→			prepareTranscriptIfNeeded(agentType, liveTranscriptPath)
   424→		}
   425→		if liveData, readErr := os.ReadFile(liveTranscriptPath); readErr == nil && len(liveData) > 0 { //nolint:gosec // path from session state
   426→			fullTranscript = string(liveData)
   427→		}
   428→	}
   429→	if fullTranscript == "" {
   430→		// Fall back to shadow branch copy
   431→		if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   432→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   433→				fullTranscript = content
   434→			}
   435→		} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   436→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   437→				fullTranscript = content
   438→			}
   439→		}
   440→	}
   441→
   442→	// Process transcript based on agent type
   443→	if fullTranscript != "" {
   444→		data.Transcript = []byte(fullTranscript)
   445→		data.FullTranscriptLines = countTranscriptItems(agentType, fullTranscript)
   446→		data.Prompts = extractUserPrompts(agentType, fullTranscript)
   447→		data.Context = generateContextFromPrompts(data.Prompts)
   448→	}
   449→
   450→	// Use tracked files from session state (not all files in tree)
   451→	data.FilesTouched = filesTouched
   452→
   453→	// Calculate token usage from the extracted transcript portion
   454→	if len(data.Transcript) > 0 {
   455→		data.TokenUsage = calculateTokenUsage(agentType, data.Transcript, checkpointTranscriptStart)
   456→	}
   457→
   458→	return data, nil
   459→}

   461→// extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript extracts session data directly from the live transcript file.
   462→// This is used for mid-session commits where no shadow branch exists yet.
   463→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript(state *SessionState) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
   464→	data := &ExtractedSessionData{}
   465→
   466→	// Read the live transcript
   467→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
   468→		return nil, errors.New("no transcript path in session state")
   469→	}
   470→
   471→	liveData, err := os.ReadFile(state.TranscriptPath)
   472→	if err != nil {
   473→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read live transcript: %w", err)
   474→	}
   475→
   476→	if len(liveData) == 0 {
   477→		return nil, errors.New("live transcript is empty")
   478→	}
   479→
   480→	fullTranscript := string(liveData)
   481→	data.Transcript = liveData
   482→	data.FullTranscriptLines = countTranscriptItems(state.AgentType, fullTranscript)
   483→	data.Prompts = extractUserPrompts(state.AgentType, fullTranscript)
   484→	data.Context = generateContextFromPrompts(data.Prompts)
   485→
   486→	// Extract files from transcript since state.FilesTouched may be empty for mid-session commits
   487→	// (no SaveStep/Stop has been called yet to populate it)
   488→	if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   489→		data.FilesTouched = state.FilesTouched
   490→	} else {
   491→		// Use the shared helper which includes subagent transcripts
   492→		data.FilesTouched = s.extractModifiedFilesFromLiveTranscript(state, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   493→	}
   494→
   495→	// Calculate token usage from the extracted transcript portion
   496→	if len(data.Transcript) > 0 {
   497→		data.TokenUsage = calculateTokenUsage(state.AgentType, data.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   498→	}
   499→
   500→	return data, nil
   501→}
   502→
   503→// countTranscriptItems counts lines (JSONL) or messages (JSON) in a transcript.
   504→// For Claude Code and JSONL-based agents, this counts lines.
   505→// For Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and JSON-based agents, this counts messages.
   506→// Returns 0 if the content is empty or malformed.
   507→func countTranscriptItems(agentType agent.AgentType, content string) int {
   508→	if content == "" {
   509→		return 0
   510→	}
   511→
   512→	// OpenCode uses export JSON format with {"info": {...}, "messages": [...]}
   513→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
   514→		session, err := opencode.ParseExportSession([]byte(content))
   515→		if err == nil && session != nil {
   516→			return len(session.Messages)
   517→		}
   518→		return 0
   519→	}
   520→
   521→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   522→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   523→		transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript([]byte(content))
   524→		if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
   525→			return len(transcript.Messages)
   526→		}
   527→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return 0
   528→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   529→			return 0
   530→		}
   531→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   532→	}
   533→
   534→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   535→	allLines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   536→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   537→	for len(allLines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(allLines[len(allLines)-1]) == "" {
   538→		allLines = allLines[:len(allLines)-1]
   539→	}
   540→	return len(allLines)
   541→}
   542→
   543→// extractUserPrompts extracts all user prompts from transcript content.
   544→// Returns prompts with IDE context tags stripped (e.g., <ide_opened_file>).
   545→func extractUserPrompts(agentType agent.AgentType, content string) []string {
   546→	if content == "" {
   547→		return nil
   548→	}
   549→
   550→	// OpenCode uses JSONL with a different per-line schema than Claude Code
   551→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
   552→		prompts, err := opencode.ExtractAllUserPrompts([]byte(content))
   553→		if err == nil && len(prompts) > 0 {
   554→			cleaned := make([]string, 0, len(prompts))
   555→			for _, prompt := range prompts {
   556→				if stripped := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(prompt); stripped != "" {
   557→					cleaned = append(cleaned, stripped)
   558→				}
   559→			}
   560→			return cleaned
   561→		}
   562→		return nil
   563→	}
   564→
   565→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   566→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   567→		prompts, err := geminicli.ExtractAllUserPrompts([]byte(content))
   568→		if err == nil && len(prompts) > 0 {
   569→			// Strip IDE context tags for consistency with Claude Code handling
   570→			cleaned := make([]string, 0, len(prompts))
   571→			for _, prompt := range prompts {
   572→				if stripped := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(prompt); stripped != "" {
   573→					cleaned = append(cleaned, stripped)
   574→				}
   575→			}
   576→			return cleaned
   577→		}
   578→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return nil
   579→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   580→			return nil
   581→		}
   582→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   583→	}
   584→
   585→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   586→	return extractUserPromptsFromLines(strings.Split(content, "\n"))
   587→}
   588→
   589→// calculateTokenUsage calculates token usage from raw transcript data.
   590→// startOffset is the line number (Claude Code) or message index (Gemini CLI)
   591→// where the current checkpoint began, allowing calculation for only the portion
   592→// of the transcript since the last checkpoint.
   593→func calculateTokenUsage(agentType agent.AgentType, data []byte, startOffset int) *agent.TokenUsage {
   594→	// No token usage information from Cursor yet
   595→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeCursor {
   596→		return nil
   597→	}
   598→
   599→	if len(data) == 0 {
   600→		return &agent.TokenUsage{}
   601→	}
   602→
   603→	// OpenCode uses JSONL with token info on assistant messages (different schema from Claude Code)
   604→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
   605→		return opencode.CalculateTokenUsageFromBytes(data, startOffset)
   606→	}
   607→
   608→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   609→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   610→		// Attempt to parse as Gemini JSON
   611→		transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript(data)
   612→		if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
   613→			return geminicli.CalculateTokenUsage(data, startOffset)
   614→		}
   615→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return empty usage
   616→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   617→			return &agent.TokenUsage{}
   618→		}
   619→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   620→	}
   621→
   622→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   623→	lines, err := transcript.ParseFromBytes(data)
   624→	if err != nil || len(lines) == 0 {
   625→		return &agent.TokenUsage{}
   626→	}
   627→	// Slice transcript lines to only include checkpoint portion
   628→	if startOffset > 0 && startOffset < len(lines) {
   629→		lines = lines[startOffset:]
   630→	}
   631→	return claudecode.CalculateTokenUsage(lines)
   632→}
   633→
   634→// extractUserPromptsFromLines extracts user prompts from JSONL transcript lines.
   635→// IDE-injected context tags (like <ide_opened_file>) are stripped from the results.
   636→func extractUserPromptsFromLines(lines []string) []string {
   637→	var prompts []string
   638→	for _, line := range lines {
   639→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   640→		if line == "" {
   641→			continue
   642→		}
   643→
   644→		var entry map[string]interface{}
   645→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &entry); err != nil {
   646→			continue
   647→		}
   648→
   649→		// Check for user message:
   650→		// - Claude Code uses "type": "human" or "type": "user"
   651→		// - Cursor uses "role": "user"
   652→		msgType, _ := entry["type"].(string) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion on interface{} from JSON
   653→		msgRole, _ := entry["role"].(string) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion on interface{} from JSON
   654→		isUser := msgType == "human" || msgType == "user" || msgRole == "user"
   655→		if !isUser {
   656→			continue
   657→		}
   658→
   659→		// Extract message content
   660→		message, ok := entry["message"].(map[string]interface{})
   661→		if !ok {
   662→			continue
   663→		}
   664→
   665→		// Handle string content
   666→		if content, ok := message["content"].(string); ok && content != "" {
   667→			cleaned := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(content)
   668→			if cleaned != "" {
   669→				prompts = append(prompts, cleaned)
   670→			}
   671→			continue
   672→		}
   673→
   674→		// Handle array content (e.g., multiple text blocks from VSCode)
   675→		if arr, ok := message["content"].([]interface{}); ok {
   676→			var texts []string
   677→			for _, item := range arr {
   678→				if m, ok := item.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
   679→					if m["type"] == "text" {
   680→						if text, ok := m["text"].(string); ok {
   681→							texts = append(texts, text)
   682→						}
   683→					}
   684→				}
   685→			}
   686→			if len(texts) > 0 {
   687→				cleaned := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(strings.Join(texts, "\n\n"))
   688→				if cleaned != "" {
   689→					prompts = append(prompts, cleaned)
   690→				}
   691→			}
   692→		}
   693→	}
   694→	return prompts
   695→}
   696→
   697→// generateContextFromPrompts generates context.md content from a list of prompts.
   698→func generateContextFromPrompts(prompts []string) []byte {
   699→	if len(prompts) == 0 {
   700→		return nil
   701→	}
   702→
   703→	var buf strings.Builder
   704→	buf.WriteString("# Session Context\n\n")
   705→	buf.WriteString("## User Prompts\n\n")
   706→
   707→	for i, prompt := range prompts {
   708→		// Truncate very long prompts for readability.
   709→		// Use rune-based truncation to avoid splitting multi-byte UTF-8 characters (e.g. CJK).
   710→		displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(prompt, 500, "...")
   711→		buf.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("### Prompt %d\n\n", i+1))
   712→		buf.WriteString(displayPrompt)
   713→		buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   714→	}
   715→
   716→	return []byte(buf.String())
   717→}

   719→// CondenseSessionByID force-condenses a session by its ID and cleans up.
   720→// This is used by "entire doctor" to salvage stuck sessions.
   721→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSessionByID(sessionID string) error {
   722→	ctx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "condense-by-id")
   723→
   724→	// Load session state
   725→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   726→	if err != nil {
   727→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to load session state: %w", err)
   728→	}
   729→	if state == nil {
   730→		return fmt.Errorf("session not found: %s", sessionID)
   731→	}
   732→
   733→	// Open repository
   734→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   735→	if err != nil {
   736→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
   737→	}
   738→
   739→	// Generate a checkpoint ID
   740→	checkpointID, err := id.Generate()
   741→	if err != nil {
   742→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   743→	}
   744→
   745→	// Check if shadow branch exists (required for condensation)
   746→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   747→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   748→	_, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   749→	hasShadowBranch := refErr == nil
   750→
   751→	if !hasShadowBranch {
   752→		// No shadow branch means no checkpoint data to condense.
   753→		// Just clean up the state file.
   754→		logging.Info(ctx, "no shadow branch for session, clearing state only",
   755→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   756→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   757→		)
   758→		if err := s.clearSessionState(sessionID); err != nil {
   759→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to clear session state: %w", err)
   760→		}
   761→		return nil
   762→	}
   763→
   764→	// Condense the session
   765→	result, err := s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
   766→	if err != nil {
   767→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to condense session: %w", err)
   768→	}
   769→
   770→	logging.Info(ctx, "session condensed by ID",
   771→		slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   772→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   773→		slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   774→	)
   775→
   776→	// Update session state: reset step count and transition to idle
   777→	state.StepCount = 0
   778→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   779→	state.Phase = session.PhaseIdle
   780→	state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   781→	state.AttributionBaseCommit = state.BaseCommit
   782→	state.PromptAttributions = nil
   783→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil
   784→
   785→	if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   786→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session state: %w", err)
   787→	}
   788→
   789→	// Clean up shadow branch if no other sessions need it
   790→	if err := s.cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused(repo, shadowBranchName, sessionID); err != nil {
   791→		logging.Warn(ctx, "failed to clean up shadow branch",
   792→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   793→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   794→		)
   795→		// Non-fatal: condensation succeeded, shadow branch cleanup is best-effort
   796→	}
   797→
   798→	return nil
   799→}

   801→// cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused deletes a shadow branch if no other active sessions reference it.
   802→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused(_ *git.Repository, shadowBranchName, excludeSessionID string) error {
   803→	// List all session states to check if any other session uses this shadow branch
   804→	allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates()
   805→	if err != nil {
   806→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list session states: %w", err)
   807→	}
   808→
   809→	for _, state := range allStates {
   810→		if state.SessionID == excludeSessionID {
   811→			continue
   812→		}
   813→		otherShadow := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   814→		if otherShadow == shadowBranchName && state.StepCount > 0 {
   815→			// Another session still needs this shadow branch
   816→			return nil
   817→		}
   818→	}

   820→	// No other sessions need it, delete the shadow branch via CLI
   821→	// (go-git v5's RemoveReference doesn't persist with packed refs/worktrees)

   824→		if errors.Is(err, ErrBranchNotFound) {
   825→			return nil
   826→		}
   827→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove shadow branch: %w", err)
   828→	}
   829→	return nil
   830→}

    14→// Content-aware overlap detection for checkpoint management.
    15→//
    16→// These functions determine whether a commit contains session-related work by comparing
    17→// file content (not just filenames) against the shadow branch. This enables accurate
    18→// detection of the "reverted and replaced" scenario where a user:
    19→// 1. Reverts session changes (e.g., git checkout -- file.txt)
    20→// 2. Creates completely different content in the same file
    21→// 3. Commits the new content
    22→//
    23→// In this scenario, the commit should NOT get a checkpoint trailer because the
    24→// session's work was discarded, not incorporated.
    25→//
    26→// The key distinction:
    27→// - Modified files (exist in parent commit): Always count as overlap, regardless of
    28→//   content changes. The user is editing session's work.
    29→// - New files (don't exist in parent): Require content match against shadow branch.
    30→//   If content differs completely, the session's work was likely reverted & replaced.
    31→
    32→// filesOverlapWithContent checks if any file in filesTouched overlaps with the committed
    33→// content, using content-aware comparison to detect the "reverted and replaced" scenario.
    34→//
    35→// This is used in PostCommit to determine if a session has work in the commit.
    36→func filesOverlapWithContent(repo *git.Repository, shadowBranchName string, headCommit *object.Commit, filesTouched []string) bool {
    37→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
    38→
    39→	// Build set of filesTouched for quick lookup
    40→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
    41→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
    42→		touchedSet[f] = true
    43→	}
    44→
    45→	// Get HEAD commit tree (the committed content)
    46→	headTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
    47→	if err != nil {
    48→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD tree, falling back to filename check",
    49→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    50→		)
    51→		return len(filesTouched) > 0 // Fall back: assume overlap if any files touched
    52→	}
    53→
    54→	// Get shadow branch tree (the session's content)
    55→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
    56→	shadowRef, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
    57→	if err != nil {
    58→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: shadow branch not found, falling back to filename check",
    59→			slog.String("branch", shadowBranchName),
    60→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    61→		)
    62→		return len(filesTouched) > 0 // Fall back: assume overlap if any files touched
    63→	}
    64→
    65→	shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
    66→	if err != nil {
    67→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get shadow commit, falling back to filename check",
    68→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    69→		)
    70→		return len(filesTouched) > 0
    71→	}
    72→
    73→	shadowTree, err := shadowCommit.Tree()
    74→	if err != nil {
    75→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: failed to get shadow tree, falling back to filename check",
    76→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
    77→		)
    78→		return len(filesTouched) > 0
    79→	}
    80→
    81→	// Get the parent commit tree to determine if files are modified vs newly created.
    82→	// For modified files (exist in parent), we count as overlap regardless of content
    83→	// because the user is editing the session's work.
    84→	// For newly created files (don't exist in parent), we check content to detect
    85→	// the "reverted and replaced" scenario where user deleted session's work and
    86→	// created something completely different.
    87→	var parentTree *object.Tree
    88→	if headCommit.NumParents() > 0 {
    89→		if parent, err := headCommit.Parent(0); err == nil {
    90→			if pTree, err := parent.Tree(); err == nil {
    91→				parentTree = pTree
    92→			}
    93→		}
    94→	}
    95→
    96→	// Check each file in filesTouched
    97→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
    98→		// Get file from HEAD tree (the committed content)
    99→		headFile, err := headTree.File(filePath)

   102→			// Deletions count as overlap because the agent's action (deleting the file)
   103→			// is being committed - we want the session context linked to this commit.
   104→			if parentTree != nil {
   105→				if _, parentErr := parentTree.File(filePath); parentErr == nil {
   106→					// File existed in parent but not in HEAD - this is a deletion
   107→					logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: deleted file counts as overlap",
   108→						slog.String("file", filePath),
   109→					)
   110→					return true
   111→				}
   112→			}
   113→			// File didn't exist in parent either - not a deletion, skip
   114→			continue
   115→		}
   116→
   117→		// Check if this is a modified file (exists in parent) or new file
   118→		isModified := false
   119→		if parentTree != nil {
   120→			if _, err := parentTree.File(filePath); err == nil {
   121→				isModified = true
   122→			}
   123→		}
   124→
   125→		// Modified files always count as overlap (user edited session's work)
   126→		if isModified {
   127→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: modified file counts as overlap",
   128→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   129→			)
   130→			return true
   131→		}
   132→
   133→		// For new files, check content against shadow branch
   134→		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(filePath)
   135→		if err != nil {
   136→			// File not in shadow branch - this shouldn't happen but skip it
   137→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: file in filesTouched but not in shadow branch",
   138→				slog.String("file", filePath),
   139→			)

   141→		}

   143→		// Compare by hash (blob hash) - exact content match required for new files
   144→		if headFile.Hash == shadowFile.Hash {

   147→				slog.String("hash", headFile.Hash.String()),
   148→			)

   150→		}

   153→			slog.String("file", filePath),
   154→			slog.String("head_hash", headFile.Hash.String()),
   155→			slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()),
   156→		)
   157→	}
   158→
   159→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesOverlapWithContent: no overlapping files found",
   160→		slog.Int("files_checked", len(filesTouched)),
   161→	)
   162→	return false
   163→}
   164→
   165→// stagedFilesOverlapWithContent checks if any staged file overlaps with filesTouched,
   166→// distinguishing between modified files (always overlap) and new files (check content).
   167→//
   168→// For modified files (already exist in HEAD), we count as overlap because the user
   169→// is editing the session's work. For new files (don't exist in HEAD), we require
   170→// content match to detect the "reverted and replaced" scenario.
   171→//
   172→// This is used in PrepareCommitMsg for carry-forward scenarios.
   173→func stagedFilesOverlapWithContent(repo *git.Repository, shadowTree *object.Tree, stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
   174→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   175→
   176→	// Build set of filesTouched for quick lookup
   177→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
   178→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
   179→		touchedSet[f] = true
   180→	}
   181→

   183→	head, err := repo.Head()
   184→	if err != nil {
   185→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD, falling back to filename check",
   186→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   187→		)
   188→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   189→	}
   190→	headCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   191→	if err != nil {
   192→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD commit, falling back to filename check",
   193→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   194→		)
   195→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   196→	}
   197→	headTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
   198→	if err != nil {
   199→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get HEAD tree, falling back to filename check",
   200→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   201→		)
   202→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   203→	}
   204→
   205→	// Get the git index to access staged file hashes
   206→	idx, err := repo.Storer.Index()
   207→	if err != nil {
   208→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to get index, falling back to filename check",
   209→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   210→		)
   211→		return hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched)
   212→	}
   213→
   214→	// Build a map of index entries for O(1) lookup (avoid O(n*m) nested loop)
   215→	indexEntries := make(map[string]plumbing.Hash, len(idx.Entries))
   216→	for _, entry := range idx.Entries {
   217→		indexEntries[entry.Name] = entry.Hash
   218→	}
   219→
   220→	// Check each staged file
   221→	for _, stagedPath := range stagedFiles {
   222→		if !touchedSet[stagedPath] {
   223→			continue // Not in filesTouched, skip
   224→		}
   225→
   226→		// Check if this is a modified file (exists in HEAD) or new file
   227→		_, headErr := headTree.File(stagedPath)
   228→		isModified := headErr == nil
   229→
   230→		// Modified files always count as overlap (user edited session's work)
   231→		// This includes deletions - if file exists in HEAD and is being deleted,
   232→		// that's the agent's work being committed.
   233→		if isModified {
   234→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: modified file counts as overlap",
   235→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   236→			)
   237→			return true
   238→		}
   239→
   240→		// For new files, check content against shadow branch
   241→		stagedHash, found := indexEntries[stagedPath]
   242→		if !found {
   243→			continue // Not in index (shouldn't happen but be safe)
   244→		}
   245→
   246→		// Get file from shadow branch tree
   247→		shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(stagedPath)
   248→		if err != nil {
   249→			// File not in shadow branch - can't verify content overlap.
   250→			// Don't assume overlap just because it's in filesTouched.
   251→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: file not in shadow tree, skipping",
   252→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   253→			)
   254→			continue
   255→		}
   256→

   258→		if stagedHash == shadowFile.Hash {
   259→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: new file content match found",
   260→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   261→				slog.String("hash", stagedHash.String()),
   262→			)
   263→			return true
   264→		}
   265→
   266→		// Hashes differ - check if there's significant content overlap.
   267→		// This distinguishes partial staging (user kept some agent content) from
   268→		// "reverted and replaced" (user wrote completely different content).
   269→		shadowContent, shadowErr := shadowFile.Contents()
   270→		if shadowErr != nil {
   271→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to read shadow content",

   273→				slog.String("error", shadowErr.Error()),
   274→			)
   275→			continue
   276→		}
   277→
   278→		// Read staged content from object store

   281→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: failed to read staged blob",
   282→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),

   284→			)
   285→			continue

   290→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   291→				slog.String("error", readerErr.Error()),
   292→			)

   294→		}

   299→				slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   300→				slog.String("error", readErr.Error()),

   310→			)

   312→		}
   313→
   314→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: new file has no significant overlap (reverted & replaced)",
   315→			slog.String("file", stagedPath),
   316→			slog.String("staged_hash", stagedHash.String()),
   317→			slog.String("shadow_hash", shadowFile.Hash.String()),
   318→		)
   319→	}

   321→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "stagedFilesOverlapWithContent: no overlapping files found",

   323→		slog.Int("files_touched", len(filesTouched)),
   324→	)
   325→	return false
   326→}
   327→
   328→// hasOverlappingFiles checks if any file in stagedFiles appears in filesTouched.
   329→// This is a fallback when content-aware comparison isn't possible.
   330→func hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
   331→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
   332→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
   333→		touchedSet[f] = true
   334→	}
   335→
   336→	for _, staged := range stagedFiles {
   337→		if touchedSet[staged] {
   338→			return true
   339→		}
   340→	}
   341→	return false
   342→}
   343→
   344→// filesWithRemainingAgentChanges returns files from filesTouched that still have
   345→// uncommitted agent changes. This is used for carry-forward after partial commits.
   346→//

   348→//   - It wasn't committed at all (not in committedFiles), OR
   349→//   - It was committed but the committed content doesn't match the shadow branch
   350→//     (user committed partial changes, e.g., via git add -p)
   351→//
   352→// Falls back to file-level subtraction if shadow branch is unavailable.
   353→func filesWithRemainingAgentChanges(
   354→	repo *git.Repository,
   355→	shadowBranchName string,
   356→	headCommit *object.Commit,
   357→	filesTouched []string,
   358→	committedFiles map[string]struct{},
   359→) []string {
   360→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   361→
   362→	// Get HEAD commit tree (the committed content)
   363→	commitTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
   364→	if err != nil {
   365→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get commit tree, falling back to file subtraction",
   366→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   367→		)
   368→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   369→	}
   370→
   371→	// Get shadow branch tree (the session's full content)
   372→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   373→	shadowRef, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   374→	if err != nil {
   375→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: shadow branch not found, falling back to file subtraction",
   376→			slog.String("branch", shadowBranchName),
   377→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   378→		)
   379→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   380→	}
   381→
   382→	shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
   383→	if err != nil {
   384→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get shadow commit, falling back to file subtraction",
   385→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   386→		)
   387→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   388→	}
   389→
   390→	shadowTree, err := shadowCommit.Tree()
   391→	if err != nil {
   392→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "filesWithRemainingAgentChanges: failed to get shadow tree, falling back to file subtraction",
   393→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   394→		)
   395→		return subtractFilesByName(filesTouched, committedFiles)
   396→	}
   397→
   398→	var remaining []string
   399→

   401→		// If file wasn't committed at all, it definitely has remaining changes

- Shadow reference: 3 git subprocess calls
- Shadow commit: 5 plumbing API calls
- Shadow tree: 5 plumbing API calls + 30-50 tree file lookups

| **Shadow commit** | **Line 967** | **Line 382** | **Line 65** | **Lines 400, 314** | 5 places |
| **Shadow tree** | **Line 972** | **Line 390** | **Line 73** | **Lines 405, 322** | 5+ places |
| Base commit | Line 341 | - | - | - | calculateSessionAttributions |

---

### **RECOMMENDATIONS FOR OPTIMIZATION**

1. **Cache shadow branch reference** once at the top of PostCommit loop
2. **Cache shadow commit object** once obtained
3. **Cache shadow tree object** once obtained
4. **Cache HEAD reference** once at top of PostCommit
5. **Cache HEAD commit object** once obtained
6. **Cache HEAD tree object** once obtained
7. **Cache parent tree** to avoid re-reading
8. **Pass trees as parameters** to functions instead of re-reading from references

This caching strategy could **reduce git operations by ~60-70%** per session during condensation.

Here's the full picture:

## Step 2: PostCommit Cache — Approach

### The Problem

During `PostCommit()`, the same git objects are read repeatedly across different functions. For a single session:

| Object | Times Read | Where |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| **Shadow ref** | **4x** | sessionHasNewContent, filesOverlapWithContent, filesWithRemainingAgentChanges, CondenseSession |
| **Shadow commit** | **5x** | same 4 + calculateSessionAttributions |
| **Shadow tree** | **5x** | same pattern |
| HEAD ref | 2x | PostCommit, calculateSessionAttributions |
| HEAD commit | 2x | PostCommit, calculateSessionAttributions |
| HEAD tree | 4x | filesChangedInCommit, filesOverlapWithContent, calculateSessionAttributions, filesWithRemainingAgentChanges |
| Parent commit+tree | 2x | filesChangedInCommit, filesOverlapWithContent |

That's **~25 redundant git object reads per session**. With 2-3 concurrent sessions, it multiplies further.

### The Approach

Create a `postCommitCache` struct with lazy-loaded fields. Read each object once, reuse everywhere. Thread it through the per-session loop.

```go
type postCommitCache struct {
    repo   *git.Repository
    
    // Computed once at PostCommit entry
    headRef    *plumbing.Reference  // repo.Head()
    headCommit *object.Commit       // repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
    headTree   *object.Tree         // headCommit.Tree()
    parentCommit *object.Commit     // headCommit.Parent(0)
    parentTree   *object.Tree       // parentCommit.Tree()
    branchName   string             // from headRef
    authorName   string             // GetGitAuthorFromRepo (reads config)
    authorEmail  string             // same
    
    // Per-session (keyed by shadow branch name)
    shadowRefs    map[string]*plumbing.Reference
    shadowCommits map[string]*object.Commit
    shadowTrees   map[string]*object.Tree
}
```

Functions like `filesOverlapWithContent`, `filesWithRemainingAgentChanges`, `calculateSessionAttributions`, and `CondenseSession` would accept the cache instead of calling `repo.Head()`, `repo.Reference()`, etc. themselves.

### Why It Makes Sense

1. **Pure win, no behavioral change.** We're caching immutable git objects — a commit hash always resolves to the same commit. There's no risk of stale data within a single PostCommit call.

2. **The reads are expensive.** Each `repo.Reference()` or `repo.CommitObject()` goes through go-git's storer, which involves hash lookups, packfile indexing, and object decompression. At ~25 redundant reads per session, this adds measurable latency.

3. **Scoped lifetime.** The cache lives only for the duration of one `PostCommit()` call, then is garbage collected. No global state, no invalidation complexity.

### Risks

1. **Large diff touching many function signatures.** `filesOverlapWithContent`, `filesWithRemainingAgentChanges`, `calculateSessionAttributions`, `CondenseSession`, `sessionHasNewContent`, and `extractSessionData` all need to accept the cache. This is the biggest risk — many functions change signature, which could introduce bugs if a parameter is threaded incorrectly.

   **Mitigation:** The existing test suite (30+ integration tests covering PostCommit/condensation) will catch regressions. We change signatures but not logic.

2. **Cache coherence within PostCommit.** If something modifies the shadow branch mid-loop (e.g., `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` creates a new shadow commit), the cached shadow commit/tree for that branch would be stale.

   **Mitigation:** `carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` happens *after* all reads for that session are done. And the cache is per-session keyed by branch name — the new branch name won't collide with the old cached entry. We need to verify this ordering carefully.

3. **Parent commit may not exist.** For initial commits (no parent), `headCommit.Parent(0)` returns an error. The cache needs to handle this gracefully (nil parent commit/tree).

   **Mitigation:** The existing code already handles this — `filesChangedInCommit` checks for the error. The cache just needs to preserve that pattern.

### Implementation Plan

1. Define `postCommitCache` struct in `manual_commit_hooks.go` with lazy accessor methods (e.g., `cache.HeadTree()` reads once, returns cached on subsequent calls)
2. Initialize at the top of `PostCommit()` with `repo`, `head`, `commit` (already read there)
3. Refactor each function to accept cache instead of reading git objects directly:
   - `filesChangedInCommit` → use `cache.HeadTree()`, `cache.ParentTree()`
   - `sessionHasNewContent` → use `cache.ShadowRef(branchName)`, `cache.ShadowTree(branchName)`
   - `filesOverlapWithContent` → use cached head tree, parent tree, shadow tree
   - `filesWithRemainingAgentChanges` → use cached head tree, shadow tree
   - `calculateSessionAttributions` → use cached head commit/tree, shadow commit/tree
   - `CondenseSession` → use cached shadow ref, author, branch name
4. Run full test suite to verify no regressions

   303→		// No new content — no trailer needed
   304→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no content to link",
   305→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   306→			slog.String("source", source),
   307→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   308→		)
   309→		return nil
   310→	}
   311→
   312→	// Read current commit message
   313→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   314→	if err != nil {
   315→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   316→	}
   317→
   318→	message := string(content)
   319→
   320→	// Check if trailer already exists (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   321→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   322→		// Trailer already exists (e.g., amend) - keep it
   323→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer already exists",
   324→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   325→			slog.String("source", source),
   326→			slog.String("existing_checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   327→		)
   328→		return nil
   329→	}
   330→
   331→	// Generate a fresh checkpoint ID
   332→	checkpointID, err := id.Generate()
   333→	if err != nil {
   334→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   335→	}
   336→
   337→	// Determine agent type and last prompt from session
   338→	agentType := DefaultAgentType // default for backward compatibility
   339→	var lastPrompt string
   340→	if len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   341→		firstSession := sessionsWithContent[0]
   342→		if firstSession.AgentType != "" {
   343→			agentType = firstSession.AgentType
   344→		}
   345→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, firstSession)
   346→	}
   347→
   348→	// Prepare prompt for display: collapse newlines/whitespace, then truncate (rune-safe)
   349→	displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(stringutil.CollapseWhitespace(lastPrompt), 80, "...")
   350→
   351→	// Add trailer differently based on commit source
   352→	switch source {
   353→	case "message":
   354→		// Using -m or -F: ask user interactively whether to add trailer
   355→		// (comments won't be stripped by git in this mode)
   356→
   357→		// Build context string for interactive prompt
   358→		var promptContext string
   359→		if displayPrompt != "" {
   360→			promptContext = "You have an active " + string(agentType) + " session.\nLast Prompt: " + displayPrompt
   361→		}
   362→
   363→		if !askConfirmTTY("Link this commit to "+string(agentType)+" session context?", promptContext, true) {
   364→			// User declined - don't add trailer
   365→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: user declined trailer",
   366→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   367→				slog.String("source", source),
   368→			)
   369→			return nil
   370→		}
   371→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   372→	default:
   373→		// Normal editor flow: add trailer with explanatory comment (will be stripped by git)
   374→		message = addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message, checkpointID, string(agentType), displayPrompt)
   375→	}
   376→
   377→	logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer added",
   378→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   379→		slog.String("source", source),
   380→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   381→	)
   382→
   383→	// Write updated message back
   384→	if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   385→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   386→	}
   387→
   388→	return nil
   389→}

   391→// handleAmendCommitMsg handles the prepare-commit-msg hook for amend operations
   392→// (source="commit"). It preserves existing trailers or restores from LastCheckpointID.
   393→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) handleAmendCommitMsg(logCtx context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error {
   394→	// Read current commit message
   395→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   396→	if err != nil {
   397→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   398→	}
   399→
   400→	message := string(content)
   401→
   402→	// If message already has a trailer, keep it unchanged
   403→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   404→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: amend preserves existing trailer",
   405→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   406→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   407→		)
   408→		return nil
   409→	}
   410→
   411→	// No trailer in message — check if any session has LastCheckpointID to restore
   412→	worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot()
   413→	if err != nil {
   414→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   415→	}
   416→
   417→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   418→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   419→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // No sessions - nothing to restore
   420→	}
   421→
   422→	// For amend, HEAD^ is the commit being amended, and HEAD is where we are now.
   423→	// We need to match sessions whose BaseCommit equals HEAD (the commit being amended
   424→	// was created from this base). This prevents stale sessions from injecting
   425→	// unrelated checkpoint IDs.
   426→	repo, repoErr := OpenRepository()
   427→	if repoErr != nil {
   428→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   429→	}
   430→	head, headErr := repo.Head()
   431→	if headErr != nil {
   432→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   433→	}
   434→	currentHead := head.Hash().String()
   435→
   436→	// Find first matching session with LastCheckpointID to restore.
   437→	// LastCheckpointID is set after condensation completes.
   438→	for _, state := range sessions {
   439→		if state.BaseCommit != currentHead {
   440→			continue
   441→		}
   442→		if state.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   443→			continue
   444→		}
   445→		cpID := state.LastCheckpointID
   446→		source := "LastCheckpointID"
   447→
   448→		// Restore the trailer
   449→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, cpID)
   450→		if writeErr := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); writeErr != nil {
   451→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   452→		}
   453→
   454→		logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: restored trailer on amend",
   455→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   456→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpID.String()),
   457→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   458→			slog.String("source", source),
   459→		)
   460→		return nil
   461→	}
   462→
   463→	// No checkpoint ID found - leave message unchanged
   464→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: amend with no checkpoint to restore",
   465→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   466→	)
   467→	return nil
   468→}

   470→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   471→// Uses the session state machine to determine what action to take per session:
   472→//   - ACTIVE → condense immediately (each commit gets its own checkpoint)
   473→//   - IDLE → condense immediately
   474→//   - ENDED → condense if files touched, discard if empty
   475→//
   476→// After condensation for ACTIVE sessions, remaining uncommitted files are
   477→// carried forward to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.
   478→//
   479→// Shadow branches are only deleted when ALL sessions sharing the branch are non-active
   480→// and were condensed during this PostCommit.
   481→
   482→// postCommitActionHandler implements session.ActionHandler for PostCommit.
   483→// Each session in the loop gets its own handler with per-session context.
   484→// Handler methods use the *State parameter from ApplyTransition (same pointer
   485→// as the state being transitioned) rather than capturing state separately.
   486→type postCommitActionHandler struct {
   487→	s                      *ManualCommitStrategy
   488→	logCtx                 context.Context
   489→	repo                   *git.Repository
   490→	checkpointID           id.CheckpointID
   491→	head                   *plumbing.Reference
   492→	commit                 *object.Commit
   493→	newHead                string
   494→	shadowBranchName       string
   495→	shadowBranchesToDelete map[string]struct{}
   496→	committedFileSet       map[string]struct{}
   497→	hasNew                 bool
   498→	filesTouchedBefore     []string
   499→
   500→	// Output: set by handler methods, read by caller after TransitionAndLog.
   501→	condensed bool
   502→}
   503→
   504→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondense(state *session.State) error {
   505→	shouldCondense := h.shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(state.Phase.IsActive())
   506→
   507→	logging.Debug(h.logCtx, "post-commit: HandleCondense decision",
   508→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   509→		slog.String("phase", string(state.Phase)),
   510→		slog.Bool("has_new", h.hasNew),
   511→		slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   512→		slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),
   513→	)
   514→
   515→	if shouldCondense {
   516→		h.condensed = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.logCtx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, h.committedFileSet)
   517→	} else {
   518→		h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.logCtx, state, h.newHead)
   519→	}
   520→	return nil
   521→}
   522→
   523→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched(state *session.State) error {
   524→	shouldCondense := len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 && h.shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(state.Phase.IsActive())
   525→
   526→	logging.Debug(h.logCtx, "post-commit: HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched decision",
   527→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   528→		slog.String("phase", string(state.Phase)),
   529→		slog.Bool("has_new", h.hasNew),
   530→		slog.Int("files_touched", len(state.FilesTouched)),
   531→		slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   532→		slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),
   533→	)
   534→
   535→	if shouldCondense {
   536→		h.condensed = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.logCtx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, h.committedFileSet)
   537→	} else {
   538→		h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.logCtx, state, h.newHead)
   539→	}
   540→	return nil
   541→}
   542→
   543→// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck returns true if the session should be condensed
   544→// into this commit. Requires both that hasNew is true AND that the session's files
   545→// overlap with the committed files with matching content.
   546→//
   547→// This prevents stale sessions (ACTIVE sessions where the agent was killed, or
   548→// ENDED/IDLE sessions with carry-forward files) from being condensed into every
   549→// unrelated commit.
   550→//
   551→// filesTouchedBefore is populated from:
   552→//   - state.FilesTouched for IDLE/ENDED sessions (set via SaveStep/SaveTaskStep -> mergeFilesTouched)
   553→//   - transcript extraction for ACTIVE sessions when FilesTouched is empty
   554→//
   555→// When filesTouchedBefore is empty:
   556→//   - For ACTIVE sessions: fail-open (trust hasNew) because the agent may be
   557→//     mid-turn before any files are saved to state.
   558→//   - For IDLE/ENDED sessions: return false because there are no files to
   559→//     overlap with the commit.
   560→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(isActive bool) bool {
   561→	if !h.hasNew {
   562→		return false
   563→	}
   564→	if len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   565→		return isActive // ACTIVE: fail-open; IDLE/ENDED: no files = no overlap
   566→	}
   567→	// Only check files that were actually changed in this commit.
   568→	// Without this, files that exist in the tree but weren't changed
   569→	// would pass the "modified file" check in filesOverlapWithContent
   570→	// (because the file exists in the parent tree), causing stale
   571→	// sessions to be incorrectly condensed.
   572→	var committedTouchedFiles []string
   573→	for _, f := range h.filesTouchedBefore {
   574→		if _, ok := h.committedFileSet[f]; ok {
   575→			committedTouchedFiles = append(committedTouchedFiles, f)
   576→		}
   577→	}
   578→	if len(committedTouchedFiles) == 0 {
   579→		return false
   580→	}
   581→	return filesOverlapWithContent(h.repo, h.shadowBranchName, h.commit, committedTouchedFiles)
   582→}
   583→
   584→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleDiscardIfNoFiles(state *session.State) error {
   585→	if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {
   586→		logging.Debug(h.logCtx, "post-commit: skipping empty ended session (no files to condense)",
   587→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   588→		)
   589→	}
   590→	h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.logCtx, state, h.newHead)
   591→	return nil
   592→}
